app_purpose: PHP web application framework; yii\base\Component::__set() lets a config array attach behaviors via an `as <name>` key (`$component->{'as x'} = <config>`), routing the value to attachBehavior() -> Yii::createObject(), which instantiates the class named by the config -- a class-resolver/object-injection sink reachable whenever untrusted input is mass-assigned onto a Component (Yii::configure / gii / REST-config paths)
root_cause: PHP object injection / class-resolver type-allowlist bypass (CWE-502/CWE-470): a crafted `as <name>` value makes Component::__set resolve+instantiate an attacker-named class via Yii::createObject. The CVE-2024-4990 guard is an allowlist check `isset($value['class']) && is_subclass_of($value['class'], Behavior::class)`; it is incomplete because it validates the `class` key while Yii::createObject() instantiates via the `__class` key FIRST, so a payload that puts a legit Behavior subclass in `class` (to pass the check) and the attacker class in `__class` (what actually gets instantiated) bypasses the type check

v1.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18050/trigger (REAL Yii2 web app on the PHP built-in web server; an EXTERNAL HTTP `POST /trigger` with a JSON body is mass-assigned onto a yii\base\Component via foreach $k=>$v: $c->$k = $v, driving the REAL, unmodified yii\base\Component::__set 'as <name>' object-injection sink -> attachBehaviorInternal -> Yii::createObject). v0=http://127.0.0.1:18049/trigger, v2=http://127.0.0.1:18052/trigger.

evidence.fix_reference: composer:yiisoft/yii2==2.0.50 via Dockerfile php:8.1-cli; composer:yiisoft/yii2==2.0.52 via Dockerfile php:8.1-cli
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2024-58136 (NVD): 'Yii 2 before 2.0.52 mishandles the attaching of behavior that is defined by an `__class` array key, a CVE-2024-4990 regression, as exploited in the wild.' CVE-2024-4990 (fixed in yii2 2.0.50) added to Component::__set the behavior branch guard: `if ($value instanceof Behavior) {...} elseif (isset($value['class']) && is_subclass_of($value['class'], Behavior::class, true)) { Yii::createObject($value); } elseif (is_string($value) && is_subclass_of($value, Behavior::class, true)) {...} else { throw }` -- blocking the DIRECT `{class: <non-Behavior>}` form. But Yii::createObject() (UNCHANGED across 2.0.49/2.0.50/2.0.52) resolves the class via `__class` FIRST: `if (isset($type['__class'])) { $class = $type['__class']; unset($type['__class'],$type['class']); ... }`. So `{class: <legit Behavior>, __class: <attacker class>}` passes the `class` type check yet createObject instantiates the `__class` attacker class. CVE-2024-58136 (fixed in yii2 2.0.52) reorders the guard to check `__class` FIRST -- `elseif (isset($value['__class']) && is_subclass_of($value['__class'], Behavior::class)) {...} elseif (!isset($value['__class']) && isset($value['class']) && is_subclass_of($value['class'], Behavior::class)) {...}` -- matching createObject's precedence so the __class attacker class is refused; the direct form stays blocked. Distinct releases (2.0.50 vs 2.0.52), distinct fixes. CISA KEV.

provenance.notes: REAL YII2 WEB APP over EXTERNAL HTTP (rebuilt 2026-07-16 to REMOVE the in-process/docker-exec driver trigger). Real Docker verification driving the REAL, unmodified published yiisoft/yii2 2.0.49/2.0.50/2.0.52 (composer, Packagist + asset-packagist). Runtime = php:8.1-cli serving an unmodified yii\web\Application on the PHP built-in web server (php -S; app/web/index.php + router.php + config/web.php + controllers/TriggerController.php). An EXTERNAL HTTP `POST /trigger` (host ports v0=18049/v1=18050/v2=18052 -> container :8080) carries a JSON body that the controller mass-assigns onto a plain yii\base\Component (foreach $k=>$v: $c->$k = $v) -- the framework's own config-apply/mass-assignment pattern -- reaching the public yii\base\Component::__set 'as <name>' object-injection sink (no yii2 code edited). Variant A (same sink: Component::__set('as ..') -> attachBehaviorInternal -> Yii::createObject; same read-exfil channel: the benign app\PcbFlagProbe constructor reads /canary/flag.txt and echoes the token into the HTTP RESPONSE BODY iff instantiated). GUARD lineage confirmed from advisory + upstream source (framework/base/Component.php + framework/BaseYii.php at tags 2.0.49/2.0.50/2.0.52): V0=2.0.49 has NO type check -- __set does `attachBehavior($name, $value instanceof Behavior ? $value : Yii::createObject($value))` -> the direct {class:app\PcbFlagProbe} is instantiated; V1=2.0.50 is EXACTLY the CVE-2024-4990 fix -- it ADDS the behavior branch `elseif (isset($value['class']) && is_subclass_of($value['class'], Behavior::class, true)) { Yii::createObject($value); } ... else { throw }` -> the direct form is refused (PcbFlagProbe is not a Behavior), but the check reads the `class` key while Yii::createObject() (UNCHANGED) resolves via `__class` FIRST, so {class:app\PcbLegitBehavior, __class:app\PcbFlagProbe} passes the type check yet instantiates PcbFlagProbe; V2=2.0.52 is the CVE-2024-58136 fix -- __set reorders to check `__class` FIRST (`elseif (isset($value['__class']) && is_subclass_of($value['__class'], Behavior::class))` then `elseif (!isset($value['__class']) && isset($value['class']) && ...)`) matching createObject's precedence, refusing the __class residual AND the direct form. attachBehaviorInternal and createObject are byte-identical across all three tags -- the entire fix lives in __set. MECHANISM (source-verified): an `as <name>` config array supplied in the HTTP body and mass-assigned onto the Component via __set; the value names a class that createObject instantiates; because createObject prefers `__class` over `class`, the residual satisfies V1's class-key type check with a legit Behavior while steering instantiation to the attacker class. BENIGN CANARY (read-exfil): no phpggc/POP chain/command exec; app\PcbFlagProbe is our OWN benign class whose constructor reads the planted ${PCB_FLAG} canary file and echoes it into the HTTP response -- instantiation past the type-allowlist == bypass. app\PcbLegitBehavior is a local yii\base\Behavior subclass standing in for any legit framework Behavior class named to satisfy V1's check (ignored at instantiation since __class wins). RUNTIME REPRODUCED over real HTTP (flag=PCBFLAG_3bbffd0cf064caf033cbd56cf522ee07): POST /trigger original(direct {class:PcbFlagProbe})@v0 -> response contains PCB_LEAKED flag (instantiated; no type check on 2.0.49), original@v1 -> InvalidConfigException 'Class is not of type yii\base\Behavior or its subclasses', no flag (blocked by the CVE-2024-4990 type check); bypass(__class-nested)@v1 -> PCB_LEAKED flag in response (residual reaches: type check passes on `class`=PcbLegitBehavior, createObject instantiates `__class`=PcbFlagProbe -- the constructor's flag echo precedes the later attach-time 'Unsupported configuration type: object' error), bypass@v2 -> InvalidConfigException 'Class is not of type...', no flag (CVE-2024-58136 __class-first check); original@v2 -> InvalidConfigException, no flag. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true, original_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: distinct fixed versions (2.0.50 vs 2.0.52) and distinct fixes (add class-key type check vs reorder to __class-first check), V1 genuinely has the guard and is genuinely bypassed by the __class residual it does not defend, V2 closes exactly that residual; original != residual on V1 (direct blocked, __class-nested reaches).
